name: Thumbcache
location: %USERPROFILE%\AppData\Local\Microsoft\Windows\Explorer (per-user; one database per thumbnail size, e.g. thumbcache_256.db)
purpose: Centralizes thumbnail images for pictures, documents, and folders into a per-user set of databases, one per thumbnail size (small/medium/large/extra large), replacing the per-folder Thumbs.db model used on Windows XP. Like Thumbs.db, it can retain evidence of a folder's prior contents after the source files are deleted.
key_fields: Thumbnail image data - an extractable copy of the original picture, document icon, or folder preview
Thumbnail Cache ID - cross-referenceable against Windows Search Database records to recover filename, path, and metadata
Database file per size tier (e.g., thumbcache_32.db, _96, _256, _1024)
normal_baseline: Thumbcache databases populated with thumbnails matching pictures, documents, and folders the user has browsed in Explorer at the view sizes actually used (e.g., large icons vs. list view).
anomalies: Thumbnail images of sensitive documents or screenshots with no corresponding source file remaining anywhere on disk
Thumbnail Cache IDs with no matching record in the Windows Search Database, suggesting the source file or its index entry was deliberately removed after the thumbnail was cached
Thumbnails present for a user account whose role gives no reason to browse the folder or content type represented

A thumbcache database unusually small or missing expected entries relative to the user's known file activity, suggesting the cache was cleared (e.g., via Disk Cleanup's 'Thumbnails' option) to remove this evidence
anti_forensic_notes: Thumbcache databases can be cleared through Disk Cleanup's 'Thumbnails' option or third-party privacy cleaners, but because thumbnails are generated lazily on first view rather than proactively for every file, a clean or sparse database is also the expected state on a system where thumbnail view was rarely used-so absence alone is not proof of clearing. The source picture or document does not need to still exist for its thumbnail to remain.
interpretation: Database files are named by pixel dimension (e.g., thumbcache_256.db), with each file holding thumbnails generated for that display size; a given source file's thumbnail can appear in more than one size database if it was viewed at multiple Explorer view settings. Each cached thumbnail carries a Thumbnail Cache ID that can be looked up in the Windows Search Database to recover the original filename, path, and metadata the Thumbcache database itself does not store, since it retains only the rendered image.
